prompt_text:
Adopt the persona of a cybersecurity threat intelligence annotation specialist.
You are conducting MODEL INFERENCE ONLY to identify named entities from the supplied text. This instruction is exclusively for generating machine-readable extraction results and is not intended for creating training data or human-reference labels.

Identify named entities from the provided text using ONLY the following four types:
- Vulnerability: must be a literal CVE identifier formatted as CVE-YYYY-NNNN (e.g., CVE-2021-44228). Known vulnerability names (like "Log4Shell", "Snake", "EternalBlue") or non-CVE descriptions must NOT be annotated as Vulnerabilities, even if they denote a known flaw. Only exact CVE-YYYY-NNNN substrings are acceptable.
- Weakness: a specific CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) or fundamental flaw class.
- Configuration: a specific product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that may be impacted by vulnerabilities. Generic filenames, IP addresses, ports, or arbitrary strings that are not clearly identifiable affected products/components must NOT be marked as Configuration (e.g., "comadmin.dat", "104.155.149[.]103", "443", "winds.exe" are excluded unless explicitly given as a product/component name).
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (e.g., T1190, T1090.002, T1078, TA0011) or explicitly named attack method. Each distinct ID occurrence must be its own entity containing only the exact ID substring (e.g., from "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)" extract "T1078" and "T0859" separately, not the whole phrase). Both sub-technique IDs (e.g., T1090.002) and parent technique IDs (e.g., T1090) are valid when explicitly present. Only exact MITRE ATT&CK T-code or TA-code substrings qualify; do NOT tag software/tool IDs such as S0508, S1063, S1054 as AttackTechnique.

Constraints:
1. All entity text MUST be an exact verbatim substring from the input text.
2. Supply 0-based start and end character offsets based on the input text. end is exclusive, so text[start:end] equals the entity text exactly.
3. For normalized_id, give the canonical identifier if available (e.g., standard CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI for products, or T-code for ATT&CK); otherwise null.
4. Do not output repeated duplicate entries for the identical mention span.
5. Extract only entities that meet the strict definitions. Skip any span that does not clearly fit one of the four types per the rules.
6. For AttackTechnique, capture solely the exact ID token (e.g., "T1090.002", "T1078") as entity text, never the surrounding descriptive words.
7. Never infer or insert entities not present as exact substrings in the input text. Do not hallucinate configurations, products, vulnerability names, or technique IDs that are not explicitly written in the provided text.
8. Output ONLY the specified JSON schema fields per entity: id, text, type, start, end, normalized_id. Do not add fields beyond the specified schema (e.g., no "evidence", "notes", or other extra keys).
9. The reference samples below include gold-standard outputs that contain "evidence" and/or "notes" keys. Those keys are STRICTLY FOR HUMAN REFERENCE IN THE EXAMPLES and MUST NOT be copied or generated in your output. Your output must never contain "evidence" or "notes" or any field outside the schema in Rule 8.

Reference Samples:
<example>
<text>
Attackers exploited CVE-2021-44228 in the Log4j component to gain initial access by exploiting a public-facing application (T1190).
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2021-44228", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 20, "end": 34, "normalized_id": "CVE-2021-44228"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "Log4j", "type": "Configuration", "start": 42, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:apache:log4j:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "T1190", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 124, "end": 129, "normalized_id": "T1190"}
]
</entities>
</example>

<example>
<text>
CVE-2021-26855 is a server-side request forgery (CWE-918) vulnerability in Microsoft Exchange Server.
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "CVE-2021-26855", "type": "Vulnerability", "start": 0, "end": 14, "normalized_id": "CVE-2021-26855"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "server-side request forgery", "type": "Weakness", "start": 20, "end": 47, "normalized_id": "CWE-918"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "CWE-918", "type": "Weakness", "start": 49, "end": 56, "normalized_id": "CWE-918"},
  {"id": "E4", "text": "Microsoft Exchange Server", "type": "Configuration", "start": 75, "end": 100, "normalized_id": "cpe:2.3:a:microsoft:exchange_server:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:*"}
]
</entities>
</example>

<example>
<text>
A TTP associated with this actor is the use of residential proxies (T1090.002). The SVR use password spraying (T1110) and valid accounts (T1078).
</text>
<entities>
[
  {"id": "E1", "text": "T1090.002", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 57, "end": 66, "normalized_id": "T1090.002"},
  {"id": "E2", "text": "T1110", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 102, "end": 107, "normalized_id": "T1110"},
  {"id": "E3", "text": "T1078", "type": "AttackTechnique", "start": 128, "end": 133, "normalized_id": "T1078"}
]
</entities>
</example>

Output JSON only. Do not add fields beyond the specified schema. Never infer or insert entities not present as exact substrings. Do not include "evidence", "notes", or any extra keys in your output under any circumstances.

Act as an expert in cybersecurity threat intelligence annotation.
From the provided text, extract named entities using EXCLUSIVELY the four categories defined below:
- Vulnerability: must be a literal CVE identifier formatted as CVE-YYYY-NNNN (e.g., CVE-2021-44228). Known vulnerability names (like "Log4Shell", "Snake", "EternalBlue") or non-CVE descriptions must NOT be labeled as Vulnerabilities, even if they denote a known flaw. Only exact CVE-YYYY-NNNN substrings are valid.
- Weakness: a specific CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) OR a fundamental flaw class explicitly described in the text as a vulnerability type (e.g., "server-side request forgery", "path traversal", "improper authentication"). If a CWE-xxx token appears, extract it as Weakness and set normalized_id to that CWE-xxx; if only a flaw class name appears without a CWE token, extract the exact phrase as Weakness and set normalized_id to the corresponding CWE if widely known or null if unspecified.
- Configuration: a specific product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that is EXPLICITLY stated in the text as affected by, targeted by, or subject to a vulnerability or attack technique (e.g., "in Microsoft Exchange Server" within a sentence describing CVE-2021-26855, or a CPE-like string). A product/component name is extracted as Configuration ONLY if the text directly presents it as an affected/targeted item (e.g., "vulnerability in X", "X affected by", "attackers used TXXXX against X", "flaw in X") OR it appears as a clear CPE-style identifier. The following are EXCLUDED and must NOT be tagged as Configuration under any circumstances:
  * Generic filenames, IP addresses, ports, or arbitrary strings not clearly identifiable as products/components (e.g., "comadmin.dat", "104.155.149[.]103", "443", "winds.exe").
  * Vendor names alone mentioned in passing (e.g., "Webroot" stated without context of being affected/targeted).
  * Cloud services or product names mentioned incidentally without explicit affected/targeted context (e.g., "Microsoft OneDrive" referenced only as a data storage location, not as a compromised component).
  * Any product/component not explicitly linked to a vulnerability or technique in the text.
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID in the form T#### (e.g., T1190, T1090.002, T1078, T1055.001) or explicitly named attack method. Each distinct ID occurrence must be its own entity containing only the exact ID substring (e.g., from "Valid Accounts (T1078)" extract "T1078" only). Both sub-technique IDs (e.g., T1090.002) and parent technique IDs (e.g., T1090) are valid when explicitly stated. IDs may appear with brackets (e.g., "[T1055.001]") or newline-separated (e.g., "T1059.001\n") – extract only the exact T-code token without brackets or whitespace. IMPORTANT: MITRE ATT&CK tactic IDs (TA####, e.g., TA0011, TA0008, TA0007, TA0005, TA0006) are NOT in evaluation scope and must NEVER be extracted as AttackTechnique or any other type. Only T-code technique IDs qualify. Do NOT tag software/tool IDs such as S0508, S1063, S1054 as AttackTechnique.

Rules:
1. All entity text MUST be an exact verbatim substring from the input text.
2. Provide 0-based start and end character offsets based on the input text. end is exclusive, so text[start:end] equals the entity text exactly.
3. For normalized_id, provide the canonical identifier if present (e.g., standard CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI for products explicitly affected/targeted, or T-code for ATT&CK); otherwise null.
4. Do not output repeated duplicate entries for the identical mention span.
5. Extract only entities that satisfy the strict definitions. Skip any span that does not clearly fit one of the four types per the rules.
6. For AttackTechnique, capture solely the exact T-code token (e.g., "T1090.002", "T1078", "T1055.001") as entity text, never the surrounding descriptive words, brackets, or TA-codes.
7. Never infer or insert entities not present as exact substrings in the input text. Do not hallucinate configurations, products, vulnerability names, or technique IDs that are not explicitly written in the provided text.
8. Output ONLY the specified JSON schema fields per entity: id, text, type, start, end, normalized_id. Do not add fields beyond the specified schema (e.g., no "evidence", "notes", or other extra keys).
9. TA#### codes (MITRE ATT&CK tactics) are explicitly out of scope and must not appear in the output under any type.
